Parties: Corio Inc. (Delaware corp., 700 Bay Road, Suite 210, Redwood City, CA 94063) as licensee/host; Commerce One, Inc. (Delaware corp., 1600 Rivera Avenue, Walnut Creek, CA 94596) as licensor. No amendments provided.

Dates: Effective Date October 29, 1999. Signed by Corio 11/5/99; Commerce One date blank. Acceptance testing to finish by Dec 30, 1999, with notice of acceptance or rejection by Dec 31, 1999 (initial test within 30 days of delivery, no later than Dec 1, 1999). Escrow agreement due within 60 days of Effective Date. Marketing fund within 6 months. Two initial Customers targeted within 60 days.

Initial term: 5 years from Effective Date.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: Auto-renews for successive 1-year periods. Either party may stop renewal by written notice at least 30 days before the end of the initial term or any 1-year renewal. Maintenance and Support continues after term while Corio pays annual fees.

Termination rights: Material breach uncured 30 days after written notice, then the non-breaching party may terminate on written notice. Immediate termination on notice if a party becomes insolvent or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Corio may terminate with a refund of fees paid if the Software is not accepted after the third Acceptance Test, and may terminate with refund of prepaid fees for uncorrectable warranty breach. Commerce One may terminate for infringement and refund pro-rated fees (8.1). No termination for convenience. Survival: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14; Corio's Customers keep access and use, and support continues if Corio pays.

Governing law: California law, excluding conflict-of-laws rules and the 1980 UN CISG. Binding AAA arbitration, one arbitrator, San Francisco County. The non-prevailing party pays the AAA fees.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: License fees, MarketSite.net access fees (Year 1; Years 2-5 and beyond) and annual maintenance fees are redacted [*]. Implementation fee is time and materials, with a cap redacted. Revenue share: Commerce One pays Corio [*] of MarketSite transaction fees; Corio pays Commerce One [*] of Application Management Revenue. None is due on the initial 3000 Software User licenses (minimum 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer). Payment terms: license fee due on acceptance; maintenance net 30 from the acceptance anniversary; revenue share quarterly, net 30 after quarter close; professional services net 30 from invoice (issued at milestones); MarketSite access due on acceptance and each anniversary. Corio bears taxes (except on Commerce One's income) and escrow costs. No stated minimum commitment beyond the 60-day, 2-Customer efforts target.

Liability caps and limits: Each party's liability is capped at the amounts actually paid by Corio for the relevant transaction in the 12 months before the cause of action was filed. Lost profits and indirect, special or consequential damages are excluded. Section 8 (IP indemnity) is excluded from both the cap and the exclusion. Commerce One indemnifies Corio and its Customers for third-party IP infringement claims.

Insurance: none.

Audit rights: Corio keeps books for at least 3 years. Commerce One may inspect via an independent CPA, once per calendar year, with reasonable notice. Commerce One bears the cost unless the underpayment exceeds 5%, in which case Corio reimburses the reasonable cost.

Assignment and change of control: Assignment requires prior written consent, including by operation of law. Either party may assign without consent in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets, unless the transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party, in which case consent is required. Violating assignments are void.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: none. All licences are nonexclusive. Commerce One must not contact Corio Customers about non-ASP licence sales unless Corio requests, and must refer inbound requests to Corio. Mutual covenant not to sue on future patents relating to the Developments.

IP ownership and licences: Commerce One retains the Software IP. Corio receives a fee-bearing, perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive licence in North America to host and sublicense; a royalty-free perpetual internal-use licence; a demonstration licence; and a resale licence (2.4). Corio may seek worldwide expansion at no added cost, and Commerce One must not unreasonably withhold permission. No reverse engineering. Corio owns the Developments unless Commerce One supports them ongoing. Section 365(n) protection applies.

Source code escrow: Escrow in California within 60 days of the Effective Date, with Corio paying the costs. Release occurs if Commerce One dissolves or ceases business, or if repeated material breach of support obligations is uncured after 60 days. Disputes get 10 business days of negotiation, then arbitration. Post-release licence: use and modify to support the Software only.

Warranties: IP and non-conflict warranties. Product warranty and virus-free warranty run 60 days from the Effective Date, no later than Dec 31, 1999. Y2K warranty. Disclaimer of implied warranties.

Anything else: Acceptance Test process: Commerce One has 15 days to cure. Support is per Exhibit C, with P1 action plan in 2 hours and P2 in 4 hours. Force majeure, subcontracting by Corio permitted, and confidentiality via a separate NDA. Exhibit D marketing cooperation is non-binding. Entire agreement clause. Exhibit A contact names are blank.

Parties: Integra LifeSciences Corporation (Delaware corp., 311 Enterprise Drive, Plainsboro, NJ 08536) and PcoMed, LLC (Colorado LLC, 105 S. Sunset Street, Longmont, CO 80501). No amendments provided.

Dates: Effective Date May 15, 2013. Signed by PcoMed May 15, 2013 and by Integra May 29, 2013. First Product Order due within 60 days of Effective Date. Integra accepts within 10 business days of receiving conforming product (Notice of Initial Acceptance, Attachment C).

Initial term: From Effective Date until the date payment is due for Minimum Payment Period 7 (each period is one year, starting on the date in the Notice of Initial Acceptance; payment due 45 days after period ends). Roughly 7 years plus 45 days from acceptance.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: No automatic renewal. Renewal only for periods and terms mutually agreed in writing (§4.2, §12.7). No non-renewal notice needed.

Termination rights: Material breach (§4.3(a)): either party, 60 days' prior written notice, unless cured within the 60 days (or, if not curable in that time, a reasonably acceptable cure plan is presented). Bankruptcy/insolvency (§4.3(b)): immediate termination by written notice. No termination for convenience. On early termination (other than for Integra breach of §5 or §8), Integra may sell inventory and complete in-process components for 18 months (§4.4(c)). Rights cease on expiry. Survival: §§2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 4.4(c), 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. Separately, PcoMed can convert exclusivity to non-exclusive (see Exclusivity).

Governing law: State of New Jersey (§12.3). Disputes (§12.4): 30 days' senior-officer negotiation, then binding arbitration in Denver, Colorado, 3-person panel (Judicial Arbiter Group, under AAA rules), each party bears its own costs.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Two milestone payments (amounts redacted [***]): first on full execution; second within 30 days after Notice of Initial Acceptance. Royalty ("Fee") of [***]% of Net Sales of Treated and Partially Treated products (separate rates for exclusive and non-exclusive status, redacted), paid quarterly within 45 days after calendar quarter end, in USD. Run Fee: flat redacted amount per run of up to 100 products, due within 30 days of each run; no charge for regulatory runs up to [***] units or four runs. Minimum Payments for Periods 1–7 (amounts redacted), due within 45 days after each period; Integra need only use commercially reasonable efforts, may top up in cash at its sole discretion, and has no liability for a shortfall. PcoMed's sole remedy is conversion to non-exclusive. Offsets: up to [***]% of third-party patent settlement costs against Fees; enforcement costs creditable against Minimum Payments or Fees; reduced Fees still count in full toward Minimums.

Liability caps and limits: No monetary cap. Mutual exclusion of special, consequential, incidental and indirect damages (§9.1), except for breaches of §3.1, §5 and §§8.1–8.2. Indemnities (§10): PcoMed covers IP infringement from its technology, breach of its warranties and product defects tied to its technology; Integra covers infringement from Integra technology, breach of its warranties and defects in Integra Products. Integra's remedy for PcoMed infringement costs is offset against Fees only.

Insurance: none.

Audit rights: PcoMed may have an independent CPA, reasonably acceptable to Integra, inspect Net Sales records once per calendar year, on reasonable notice, at PcoMed's cost. Records are kept per Integra's retention policy. PcoMed reports results within 60 days. Underpayments are paid within 60 days after agreement or final judgment (§6.2).

Assignment and change of control: Consent required for assignment, but not for assignment to an Affiliate (assignor stays liable) or in a merger or sale of all or substantially all of the relevant assets (assignee assumes liabilities) (§12.12). No change-of-control clause.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: PcoMed grants Integra and its Affiliates sole and exclusive worldwide rights in the Field (spinal interbody/intervertebral) (§3.1). Territory is worldwide for 36 months after Notice of Initial Acceptance. Thereafter the PRC may be excluded if Integra has had no sales there; PcoMed must give 60 days' notice before using a third party. Integra may not apply other coatings (except for identification or sterilization) (§3.3). PcoMed may convert to non-exclusive after written notice and a 45-day uncured breach (§3.2). No employee or customer non-solicit. PcoMed rep that a named employee's non-compete (redacted) does not block his employment.

IP ownership and licences: Each party keeps its own technology. Joint inventions belong to PcoMed if primarily about PcoMed Technology, or to Integra if primarily about Integra Products. PcoMed alone files and prosecutes patents at its own cost. No right to manufacture with the technology. Enforcement is split by whether the infringement relates exclusively to PcoMed technology (90-day response period; 6-month follow-up).

Source code escrow: none.

Warranties: Mutual authority and no-conflict reps. PcoMed warrants title, no prior grants, no infringement (knowledge-based) and no litigation; Integra gives similar reps. No time limits stated; no product warranty period.

Anything else: Confidentiality lasts the term plus 20 years (§5.1). Terms of the Agreement are confidential. Force majeure excludes payment obligations. Use of names needs consent. Entire agreement clause. Fee and dollar figures are redacted in the filing.

Parties: Purolator Courier Ltd. ("Purolator") and Parcelway Courier Systems Canada Ltd., a subsidiary of Dynamex Inc. ("Dynamex"). Independent contractors (s.33); no partnership, JV or agency.

Dates: Made 20 November 1995 (signature dated 11/20/95; some signature blocks illegible/unsigned). Effective on that date. No amendments provided.

Initial term: Indefinite, until terminated under the agreement (s.2.1).

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: none (no renewal mechanism; evergreen).

Termination rights: (1) Without cause: either party, 2 years' written notice (s.19.1). (2) Change in control of a party: other party may terminate on written prior notice, no period stated (s.19.2). (3) Event of Default (s.17.1): bankruptcy petition not dismissed within 60 days; asset sale/winding up; ceasing business; insolvency/receiver; CCAA; execution against property; more than 3 Monthly Performance Failures in any 12 months (s.16.1); other breach uncured 30 days after written notice. Remedy: terminate on 120 days' written notice, but immediately on written notice for the performance-failure and uncured-breach defaults (17.2(a)); recover money due; repossess own property and Freight without notice. (4) Immediate termination if Dangerous Goods training certificates are not provided (s.13.2). (5) Reputation harm: other party may terminate on notice it deems appropriate (s.41).

Governing law: Ontario laws; Ontario courts, parties attorn (s.36). Disputes go to binding arbitration in Metropolitan Toronto under the Arbitration Act: single arbitrator appointed within 10 business days (fallback: President of the Arbitrators' Institute of Canada Inc.), costs split equally, arbitration is a condition precedent to any action (s.39).

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Each party pays the other per rate Schedules D (Purolator pays Dynamex) and E (Dynamex pays Purolator); the schedules' rates are not included in the text. Invoices twice monthly (15th and month-end), with supporting documents (bills of lading not required); delivered within 3 days; payable net 15 days. Interest at CIBC Toronto Main Branch prime on amounts overdue 30+ days. Services zero-rated for GST (interlining). Currency CAD. On-time performance minimum 90% monthly. Penalty after more than 3 failures in 12 months: 5 × (90% − actual %) × shipments × average yield (example: $250). Tender commitments: Purolator tenders all sameday requests to Dynamex; Dynamex tenders all overnight/next-day/multi-day requests to Purolator (3.7, 3.8). No minimum fees.

Liability caps and limits: Loss/damage/delay to Freight liability is capped at the other party's contractual liability to its customers: $4.41/kg or $2.00/lb unless a higher value is declared (s.6.3). Indemnity (s.8) is mutual, applies even if caused by the indemnitor's negligence, and is capped at the s.9 insurance coverage (8.2). Payment of claims is due within 45 days of documentation, with set-off rights (s.7). No liability for improper packing, and none for Dangerous Goods without actual prior knowledge (s.13.1). Force majeure excuses delay.

Insurance: Each party carries cargo liability of at least $100,000 per occurrence and auto/general/property liability of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence. Other party as additional insured, cross-liability clause, waiver of subrogation. Certificates before start and annually, with 30 days' notice of cancellation or change. Subcontractors must carry at least the same.

Audit rights: Performance reports and books and records are open to the other party on request; either party may request validation by an agreed auditor (s.14).

Assignment and change of control: No sale, assignment, subcontracting or transfer without prior written consent (s.23). Subcontract terms must be equivalent or higher. Change of control gives the other party a termination right (s.19.2). Binding on successors and assigns (s.32).

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: Purolator may not solicit next-day/multi-day freight from existing Dynamex sameday customers (3.5); Dynamex may not solicit overnight freight from Purolator customers (3.6); both exclude joint marketing; no stated duration. Dynamex may not provide sameday services for other next-day/multi-day carriers (3.9), except Alltours up to $5,000/month. Any similar agreement in Canada or the US requires the other party's written consent (3.11); Dynamex may contract in the US if Purolator's service is not impaired. Post-termination non-compete: 6 months after termination for default; 12 months after termination for change of control, binding the party whose control changed (s.42). No employee non-solicit.

IP ownership and licences: Each party keeps its trade-marks, colours and designs and may use the other's only with written consent and only for the services (s.35).

Source code escrow: none.

Warranties: Each party warrants capacity and authority, no breach of law or agreements, licences in good standing, and no material pending litigation (s.21 and 20.2). No time limits.

Anything else: Confidentiality of the agreement's contents (s.34); public announcements require mutual agreement (s.38); force majeure notice required (s.22); strike contingency allows subcontracting (s.15); 30 days' notice of licence changes (s.10); Dangerous Goods compliance under the TDGA (s.13); time is of the essence; entire agreement with order of precedence of Agreement, then Schedules, then the operating plan; amendments only in writing; remedies cumulative; English-language clause; monthly operational meetings. Drafting errors include the s.42 numbering (shown as 32.1), the 17.1(c) cross-reference and "Monthly Performance Failures" terminology.

Parties: Virtual Item Processing Systems, Inc. ("VIP"), 2525 NW Expressway, Suite 105, Oklahoma City, OK 73112 (Oklahoma corporation; provider). Brokers National Life Assurance Company ("BNL"), 7010 Hwy. 71 W., Suite 100, Austin, TX 78735 (Arkansas-domiciled insurer; customer).

Dates: Executed as of May 1, 2006 (Effective Date). Signed by VIP May 17, 2006 and BNL May 18, 2006. No amendments provided.

Initial term: One year from May 1, 2006.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: Auto-renews year to year (Extended Terms) unless either party gives written notice at least six (6) months before the end of the Initial Term or the then-current Extended Term. If BNL terminates during an Extended Term with less than 6 months' notice, it owes a cancellation fee: the greatest of (i) Minimum Fee x remaining months, (ii) average monthly billings over the prior 6 months x remaining months, or (iii) $30,000.

Termination rights: For cause by the non-breaching party: (A) BNL non-payment uncured 30 days after written notice (disputed billings: VIP must offer a meeting before arbitration, litigation or termination, and BNL must pay the undisputed part); (B) other material breach uncured 30 days after written notice; (C) insolvency, bankruptcy, receivership, assignment for creditors. No termination for convenience other than non-renewal notice (6 months) or the paid early cancellation above. On termination VIP gives BNL data copies at BNL's direction, at $100/hr programming and $150/hr computer processing. After notice of termination, non-routine services are billed as additional services at Schedule A termination rates (consultation $100/hr, programming $185/hr, computer time $250/hr). BNL must return VIP software and manuals.

Governing law: Oklahoma, without regard to conflict of laws. Venue for litigation: federal or state courts in Austin, Texas or Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Disputes go to binding AAA arbitration (three arbitrators, one chosen by each party plus a neutral AAA-appointed chair; location set by the arbitrators; injunctive relief claims excluded). Prevailing party recovers attorneys' fees and costs.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Minimum Fee $5,000/month. Schedule B: $.305 per policy per month (all BNL plans); renewal-year fees are billed monthly in advance. Invoices are due within 10 days of postmark; late charge 1.5%/month or the legal maximum, whichever is less. Extra lines/devices: $200 per line and adapter, $25 per visual station, $25 per printer under 299 LPM, $150 per printer over 299 LPM, per month. The base includes 1 line and up to 70 devices. BNL pays pass-through expenses (forms, phone, travel, postage, COM; some need prior written approval), its pro rata share of backup storage, and its own Equipment. Schedule A additional services: $50–$100/hr for most work (junior programmer $85, computer time $150, bank drafts $0.06 each). After the first 12 months VIP may raise rates on 30 days' notice, capped at 10% per year. New products require a written addendum with fees.

Liability caps and limits: Both parties exclude consequential, exemplary, special, indirect, incidental and punitive damages. VIP's cap is the amount BNL paid for the specific service in the 12 months before the claim accrued (or the first-12-month minimum fees if the claim accrues in the first year). Exceptions: IP infringement indemnity (8(B)) and BNL Data confidentiality (6(A)). BNL's cap is the same, except for minimum and other fees under ¶5, 15(a) and 15(c) and breach of VIP's proprietary rights. Indemnities: BNL indemnifies VIP for BNL acts, omissions and information. VIP indemnifies BNL for US IP infringement claims, and for its own acts, omissions and information (subject to the caps). Claims must be brought within 2 years of accrual. VIP is not liable for the causes listed in 9(G) (third-party hardware or software, BNL data errors, BNL breach, late error reporting) or for force majeure.

Insurance: VIP maintains property insurance sufficient to replace its hardware, software, data and facilities, plus disaster/business interruption insurance for alternate-site processing. Evidence is provided on written request. BNL has no insurance requirement.

Audit rights: none.

Assignment and change of control: No assignment, subcontracting or delegation without the other party's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). Binds successors and assigns. Change of control: none.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: none. VIP may serve other clients with the same personnel.

IP ownership and licences: VIP owns the VIP System and enhancements. BNL has a non-exclusive licence to use it online during the term, which ends at termination. BNL owns BNL Data, which is returned at termination. VIP may keep work papers and copies. VIP may use BNL's name in client advertising.

Source code escrow: none.

Warranties: VIP warrants it is duly organized, has no conflicting contracts, owns the System rights and does not infringe US patents or other IP, performs services in a workmanlike manner, and the System has no time-limit lockout. Other warranties are disclaimed, including merchantability and fitness. No stated time limits. Platform changes do not end warranties, and VIP pays BNL's resulting costs.

Anything else: Service hours are 7am–5pm Central, Mon–Fri. Backup site is provided if downtime exceeds 2 consecutive working days. Daily offsite backups. Force majeure (VIP-favourable). BNL is responsible for its own security choices. Entire agreement clause; amendments must be in writing. No third-party beneficiaries. Notices are deemed given 3 days after mailing (the text says "three (2)"). Survival of confidentiality and indemnity provisions.

Parties: VerticalNet, Inc. ("VNI") and VerticalNet Enterprises LLC (formerly Tradeum, Inc., d/b/a VerticalNet Solutions; "VNE"), together "Vert", and Converge, Inc. ("Converge"). Services are provided by VNE. Related to the Amended and Restated Subscription License Agreement (SLA) among the same parties.

Dates: Signed October 9, 2001; effective October 1, 2001. Initial Term ends March 31, 2003. No amendments provided.

Initial term: Effective Date to March 31, 2003. It continues past that date only for uncompleted Work Plan services or obligations (including payment), solely for that Work Plan.

Renewal and notice to stop renewal: No auto-renewal. Renewal only by mutual written agreement, for up to three additional one-year Renewal Terms. Renewal fees are set by mutual agreement (4.2). No notice period for non-renewal. A "Vert Non-Renewal Election" (Vert unwilling to renew on existing terms) ends the Section 8 non-solicit as to VNE Service Personnel. A "Converge Non-Renewal Election" (Vert willing, Converge declines) leaves Converge whatever SLA rights exist.

Termination rights: No termination for convenience. Events of Default: (a) insolvency, bankruptcy, involuntary proceedings not dismissed in 60 days, or general assignment for creditors; (b) material breach causing substantial deprivation, uncured 30 days after written notice (extended to 60 days if curable but not reasonably curable in 30 and cure efforts began within 30); (c) Converge nonpayment, uncured 3 Business Days after written notice. The non-defaulting party may terminate by written notice within 10 Business Days after the Event of Default. The Agreement terminates automatically if the SLA is terminated as permitted. On termination, confidential information is returned or destroyed, except where Converge's SLA licences survive.

Governing law: Laws of the United States and the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (as for agreements between Pennsylvania residents performed wholly in Pennsylvania; conflicts rules excluded). UN CISG excluded. Jury trial waived. Actions must be commenced within 2 years of accrual unless local law bars the limit.

Fees, minimum fees and commitments: Initial Term Minimum Fee $4,500,000, paid in 18 monthly instalments of $250,000. The first is due at signing, then by the 1st of each month (Nov 2001 through Mar 2003). Instalments are non-refundable. The Quarterly Allocation (Exhibit C) is 1,920 estimated hours for the team. Problem Reports and Maintenance Updates are provided even beyond the allocation. Out-of-scope services are charged at VNE's then-current time rates or per the SOW. Expenses are reimbursed. Other invoices are monthly in arrears, due in 30 days, in USD without setoff. Late charge is the lesser of 1.5% per month or the legal maximum. Converge bears sales/use taxes. Withholding gross-up applies if Converge becomes a foreign person. Converge pays extra costs if it requests an over-high severity level or the problem is not an Error. Remote connectivity costs are split equally.

Liability caps and limits: Mutual exclusion of special, incidental, exemplary and consequential damages, including lost profits. Vert is not responsible for data loss or interruption. Cap per party: (i) for Enhancements, amounts paid for that Enhancement; (ii) for Maintenance and Support, amounts paid in the 3 months before the claim arose. The cap is in addition to fees due, and VNI and VNE share one collective cap. Exceptions: bodily injury or tangible property damage from willful misconduct or gross negligence, breach of confidentiality, and court-awarded interest. Remedies in this Agreement are exclusive for Maintenance Update, Enhancement and Services claims, while SLA remedies govern product claims. Mitigation duty applies. No liability to third parties not involved in delivery.

Insurance: none

Audit rights: none

Assignment and change of control: Either party may assign to an Affiliate. Otherwise, prior written consent is required (not to be unreasonably withheld). Merger, change of Control or transfer by operation of law is not an assignment. Control means 50% or more of voting securities, or the right to control policy.

Exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicitation: No exclusivity or non-compete (non-exclusive, 10.11). Mutual employee/individual contractor non-solicit for the Term plus 1 year. General postings and unsolicited inquiries are allowed. Converge is released as to VNE Service Personnel upon a Vert Non-Renewal Election. No customer non-solicit.

IP ownership and licences: Vert solely owns Converge-Requested Enhancements, except Converge-Independent Materials, Converge Brand Features and Third-Party Materials, unless a Work Plan or SOW says otherwise. Converge grants Vert an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to the Converge-Independent Materials and Third-Party Materials (source and object code), to the extent Converge has the right. Converge's licence to Maintenance Updates and Enhancements is governed by the SLA. Vert has no obligation to deliver source code except as the SLA provides. Converge pays for third-party technology licences.

Source code escrow: none in this Agreement (source code rights are only as the SLA provides).

Warranties: Services are performed to generally-accepted industry standards. Breach must be reported in writing within 90 days of performance. Sole remedy is repair, replacement or re-performance at no cost, within 30 days where technically feasible. All other warranties (including merchantability, fitness, non-infringement) are disclaimed. Vert does not guarantee error-free operation.

Anything else: Support Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET on Support Days. Converge provides Level 1 support, VNE provides Levels 2 and 3, and Converge has at most 7 support contacts. Severity response times (Exhibit B): Sev 1 initial response in 30 minutes, 24x7 effort, status every 24 hours, final fix within 24 hours. Sev 2 initial response in 2 hours, final fix within 72 hours. Sev 3 response by next Support Day, resolution target 5 Support Days. Sev 4 diagnosis in 5 Support Days, fixed in a future Update. Converge should install Updates within about 90 days. VNE must give an Environment and Deployment Process draft within 30 days. Proposed SOWs are due within 45 days of a request. Confidentiality applies (agreement terms confidential; SEC filing redaction process, 5 Business Days). Force majeure applies. Notices go to the General Counsel (VNI at Horsham, PA, with a copy to Morgan Lewis; Converge at Peabody, MA). Integration with the SLA, amendment only by signed writing, and no third-party beneficiaries. Key personnel are named (Decker, Ahmad, Swank, DeMarchis). The execution copy is unsigned. Section 10.9 internally cites "11.9" and 9.7 cites Section 5 for payments, which appear to be drafting errors.
